text:
Alex K: @here seeing elevated 95th latency for text-gen in eu-central since ~03:32 UTC, errors on provider-a backend. spikes on long-seq routes. immediate impact on customer sessions. paging Nora.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2028-421 - eu-central provider-a latency / partial errors. severity: P1. Assigned: oncall-sre.
Nora: I'm on it. first pass — is this across all models or specific to bigger ones?
Alex K: looks worse for models > 2k tokens and rerank. small prompt traffic seems mostly fine. CPU/GPU metrics for provider-a show high scheduling waits.
Sarah P: customer reports incoming: 3 mid-market apps saw 5-10% error spikes and elevated tail latency. Sam, heads up for support escalation.
Sam (Support): Got the customer pings. I'll prepare a brief message: "We are investigating higher latencies in EU; engineering working on mitigation; no data loss expected". Any ETA?
Nora: Short-term plan: 1) soft-drain provider-a eu-central for long-seq/compute-heavy routes. 2) reroute long-seq to provider-b in eu-west until healthy. 3) apply per-route soft-rate-limit on /v1/generate and /v1/rerank for non-enterprise tenants to reduce overload. 4) pause image-enhancement feature for EU (that flows heavy GPU ops).
Mike: Can we do a non-disruptive soft-drain? I can run the drain command to stop new long-seq sessions landing on provider-a but let short sessions finish. Proposed: `redwoodctl drain --backend provider-a --region eu-central --mode soft --filter "seq_len>2000||route in (\"/v1/rerank\")"`
Nora: That looks good. Also enable fallback routing: `routingctl set policy eu-central long-seq -> provider-b eu-west priority=high failover=true`
Alex K: Rolling that now. Command output: ```
$ redwoodctl drain --backend provider-a --region eu-central --mode soft --filter "seq_len>2000||route in (\"/v1/rerank\")"
initiating soft drain
active long sessions allowed to finish: 42
new long sessions redirected: yes
expected transition window: 3-6m
```
Nora: Applying routing policy next.
Mike: Policy applied. Verified via `routingctl get policy eu-central`: shows long-seq target provider-b with immediate failover.
ops-bot: Alert: traffic shift detected: ~18% of long-seq tokens now routed to provider-b (eu-west).
Nora: Now rate-limiting non-enterprise tenants on heavy routes to curb burst: `quotactl update /v1/generate --region eu-central --plan free,standard --tokens-per-minute 50000` and `quotactl update /v1/rerank --region eu-central --plan free,standard --qps 2`
Alex K: Done. Quota updates took effect. We'll watch customer impact — enterprise plans unchanged.
Sam (Support): Messaging update sent to affected customers and support channels. Quick FAQ: explain temporary routing and rate-limits, expected restoration in 30-60 minutes.
Sarah P: Any metric on error rate drop after reroute?
Nora: Errors for long-seq on provider-a dropped from 5.4% -> 0.6% over 4m after soft-drain. Overall eu-central tail latency 95th reduced from 1.9s -> 1.2s. Non-enterprise throttles trimmed token throughput ~12%.
Mike: There's a secondary degradation on provider-b where KV-cache warmup causes short blips. I'm warming caches and increasing burst capacity there: `infractl scale provider-b eu-west --burst 20% --cache-warmup on`
Alex K: We should avoid full failover to another region if possible — looking to keep localized in EU.
Nora: Agreed. If provider-b stabilizes we'll keep long-seq routed there and un-drain provider-a gradually after provider-a clears backlog and scheduler waits subside.
ops-bot: Health check summary (eu-central): provider-a: degraded (partial drain active). provider-b: degraded->stabilizing (cache warmup). control-plane: healthy.
Sam (Support): Support queue cleared the highest-severity tickets; 2 customers still in live chat pending resolution.
Sarah P: Preparing post-incident note: would be good to include sequence-length distribution, routing decisions, and why image-enhancement was paused. Also action items for provider onboarding checklist.
Nora: Action items: 1) provider-a call with infra team to investigate scheduler backpressure (owner: Mike) 2) add canary traffic test for long-seq before cutover to new provider (owner: Alex) 3) tune cache-warmup logic for provider-b (owner: Mike) 4) update runbook to include soft-drain + per-route throttles (owner: Nora).
Alex K: Handoff: Nora you're primary for the next hour; I'm stepping out. I'll monitor logs but handoff to you.
Nora: On-call handover noted. I'll keep this channel updated. Current status: mitigation in place, customer impact limited, ETA for full stabilization 30-45m.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2028-421 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 30m.
Sam (Support): I'll add follow-up customer notes and close pending chats after stabilization.
Nora: Thanks team. Closing thread when provider-a fully un-drained and all metrics normalized.
Alex K: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
